reasoning_content:
I have enough now. Let me draft the five short bullets, targeting 200 words, never exceeding 280 words. Let me count carefully.

Key content:
1. Allow-list change: `enabled_skills` allow-list over bundled catalog, defaulting to 11 `defaultEnabled` entries from @openhands/extensions (extensions#485 shipped Phase 0). `disabled_skills` remains for user/project skills. Previously every catalog skill (~60) was baked into agent_context.skills — the reported issue. add-javadoc and bitbucket skills off by default. Fixes #16302.

2. Two important implementation files: src/utils/skill-enablement.ts (single decision point: isCatalogSkill, buildSkillEnablementFilter, migrateSkillEnablement, findInvokedCatalogSkill) and src/hooks/use-skill-enablement.ts (shared toggle hook for Customize page and conversation drawer, decides which list a skill belongs to; auto-save; deny-veto clause). Actually use-migrate-enabled-skills.ts and agent-server-adapter.ts are also candidates. The user said "two important implementation files selected from src/utils/skill-enablement.ts, src/hooks/use-skill-enablement.ts, src/hooks/use-migrate-enabled-skills.ts, src/api/agent-server-adapter.ts". I selected skill-enablement.ts and use-skill-enablement.ts. Good.

3. Test runner: Vitest — `npx vitest run` → 5064 passed, one unrelated pre-existing failure (dev-with-automation SIGHUP cleanup) which also fails on main. npm run lint and npm run check-translation-completeness clean, 4 new keys translated in 15 locales. Attribute to upstream PR report.

4. New test files: __tests__/utils/skill-enablement.test.ts (resolve/deny-veto/every migration branch), __tests__/hooks/use-migrate-enabled-skills.test.tsx (one-shot, cloud skip, no write over failed settings load), plus route and facet cases. Also agent-server-adapter.test.ts flipped assertions so add-javadoc is NOT in agent context — that flip is the fix.

5. Remaining uncertainty: follow-ups phase 3: per-workspace scoping (needs SDK WorkspacesClient schema change), cloud parity (server-side catalog un-filtered), and agent-profile disabled_skills deny-list is a second independent list the adapter never consults — which wins unresolved. Also note I referenced the PR report for Vitest/lint/translations; I did not personally run tests.

Draft:

**1. Allow-list change.** PR #16860 replaces the "all skills on" default with `enabled_skills`, an explicit allow-list over the bundled `@openhands/extensions` catalog, defaulting to the 11 entries the catalog flags `defaultEnabled` (Phase 0 shipped in extensions#485, pins 0.18.0). Only the 11 render enabled (59 cards, 48 off); `add-javadoc` and `bitbucket*` — the skills from issue #16302 — now start disabled. `disabled_skills` still governs user/project skills from `.agents/skills/`.

**2. Implementation files.** `src/utils/skill-enablement.ts` is the single decision point: `buildSkillEnablementFilter`, `migrateSkillEnablement` (one-shot), and `findInvokedCatalogSkill` (a leading slash command loads that skill regardless of lists). `src/hooks/use-skill-enablement.ts` is the shared toggle hook replacing duplicate hydrate/auto-save logic in Customize and the drawer, so one surface can't write a preference the other can't see.

**3. Test runner.** Upstream PR report: `npx vitest run` → 5064 passed with one pre-existing unrelated failure (`dev-with-automation` SIGHUP cleanup, also fails on main); lint and translation-completeness checks clean, 4 new keys in all 15 locales.

**4. New tests.** `__tests__/utils/skill-enablement.test.ts` (resolve, deny-veto, every migration branch) and `__tests__/hooks/use-migrate-enabled-skills.test.tsx` (one-shot, cloud skip, no write on failed settings load), plus route/facet cases. Adapter tests flipped to assert `add-javadoc` is absent — the flip is the fix.

**5. Uncertainty.** Phase-3 follow-ups: per-workspace scoping needs an SDK `WorkspacesClient` schema change; cloud is untouched (server-side catalog); and the agent-profile `disabled_skills` deny-list — a second, independent list the adapter never consults — has no decided winner. I did not personally run any tests; Vitest/lint/translation claims are attributed to the PR report.
